subject: Tenant-level TTL & CAIQ/SIG evidence for LumenBridge
messages:
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@lumenbridge.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: LumenBridge Legal <legal@lumenbridge.com>
Date: 2026-06-22T09:12:00Z
Subject: Tenant-level TTL question + SIG/CAIQ evidence request

Hi Chloe / Jordan,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Before we move into procurement, our security team needs clarity on two items related to retention and deletion for LumenBridge tenant data:

1) Can Redwood enforce tenant-scoped retention (e.g., 30 days) for all inference and debug logs generated by our production tenant, including KV/cache artifacts and request/response traces? We need a firm SLA for automated deletion and proof that deleted records cannot be recovered.

2) For SIG/CAIQ purposes, please attach the specific evidence artifacts you can provide showing the deletion workflow, audit logging of deletes, and a sample attestation or checksum-based proof-of-delete. Our legal team also wants to understand exceptions: what happens during a legal hold or for SOC 2 incident investigations.

Attached is a short questionnaire from our security team (LumenBridge_Retention_Questionnaire.pdf). Can you confirm a) whether tenant TTLs are supported on hosted Dedicated or only on Private deployments, b) expected timeline to produce evidence, and c) whether Redwood can run a one-off proof-of-delete export for a sample tenant?

Appreciate a concise matrix we can share with legal.

Best,
Sanjay Rao
Head of Infrastructure, LumenBridge

Attachment: LumenBridge_Retention_Questionnaire.pdf (pdf, 12KB)

From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@lumenbridge.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, LumenBridge Legal <legal@lumenbridge.com>
Date: 2026-06-22T10:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Tenant-level TTL question + SIG/CAIQ evidence request

Hi Sanjay — thanks for the clear asks and the questionnaire. Looping in Naomi from Security & Compliance for the formal artifact side and Jordan for the runtime/engineering notes.

Quick summary up front: yes, we support tenant-scoped TTLs for inference request/response logs and debug traces. The exact enforcement path depends on deployment mode (hosted Dedicated vs Private). Below is an initial mapping; we'll follow up with the evidence pack.

- Hosted (multi-tenant) API: configurable retention at product-route level; per-tenant TTLs are available via Dedicated capacity or Private deployments where tenant isolation is enforced.
- Dedicated: supports reserved-capacity tenant TTLs using segregated storage and lifecycle jobs — TTL enforcement window is up to 24 hours after expiry for deletion jobs.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): we can provide tenant-configurable TTLs and direct access to deletion proofs/logs; enforcement is immediate once the retention job runs per the configured cron.

Next steps I propose:
1) Jordan to provide a concise technical matrix (attached) listing which log categories are TTL-controlled and where deletion-proof artifacts live.
2) Naomi to pull SIG/CAIQ snippets and a templated proof-of-delete attestation.
3) Schedule a short 30-minute workshop next week to demo a sample proof-of-delete run on a staging tenant.

Jordan / Naomi — can you confirm target delivery by EOD Friday (2026-06-26) for the pack (matrix + SIG doc + workflow) and whether we can run a single proof-of-delete before Monday?

Thanks —
Chloe Martin
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_retention_matrix.csv (csv, stub)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>, Sanjay Rao <sanjay@lumenbridge.com>

Subject: Re: Tenant-level TTL question + SIG/CAIQ evidence request

On Tue, Jun 22, 2026 at 09:12 Sanjay Rao <sanjay@lumenbridge.com> wrote:
> Hi Chloe / Jordan,
>
> Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Before we move into procurement, our security team needs clarity on two items related to retention and deletion for LumenBridge tenant data:
> ...

Thanks for the clear brief, Sanjay. A few concrete technical points to help your security team map requirements to implementation:

- What we remove with TTL jobs: request/response payloads (text tokens), request metadata (timestamps, model/version, route), ephemeral KV/cache shards, and debug session traces.
- What we do not delete automatically: immutable billing records and aggregated telemetry used for platform health; these are stored in a different retention bucket and can be redacted per-contract if required.
- Proof-of-delete mechanics: when a TTL job executes we record a delete event with a unique op-id and object checksums. We can export a signed JSONL sample containing op-id, object-snapshot-hash, deletion-timestamp, and storage-ark path for a provided sample tenant. That export is signed by our keys (we include cert thumbprint) and time-stamped to serve as proof for auditors.
- Legal hold flow: legal holds suspend TTL jobs for the impacted tenant id(s) and lock the deletion artifacts behind a hold-tag; these holds are recorded in the audit log and require Security+Legal to release. We can provide the release/hold audit trail for a given window.

Operational constraints / timeline: for Hosted Dedicated we can prepare the export + signed sample proof within 3 business days. For Private deployments we can do it same-day if we have admin access to the customer's control plane.

I'll prepare a short example export (proof_of_delete_workflow.md) and a sample signed JSONL file for the workshop. Chloe / Naomi — FYI I'll need the tenant id you want used for the demo and confirmation that this will be run in staging.

— Jordan
Principal Engineer, Inference Runtime

Attachment: proof_of_delete_workflow.md (md, stub)

Regards,
Naomi Feldman
